interest: Shows 1932 Tokyo Boy Scouts' Armistice Day peace address to the US Embassy, which Grew saw as hopeful internationalism.
overview: Despatch (Nov 1932): Grew reports fourteen Tokyo Boy Scouts presented a peace address at the US Embassy on Armistice Day, which he read as a sign of Japanese youth seeking global community rather than insularity.

people.name: Kiyota Hashimoto
people.role: Representative of the Seinan Boy Scouts

subfiles.about: A diplomatic despatch from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reporting on an Armistice Day visit to the American Embassy by a delegation of Tokyo Boy Scouts.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports fourteen Tokyo Boy Scouts visited the Embassy on Armistice Day with a peace address, seeing it as a sign Japanese youth wanted global belonging.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 191 from Joseph C. Grew to the Secretary of State regarding Address presented by Japanese Boy Scouts

subfiles.about: An address delivered by the Seinan Boy Scouts to the American Embassy conveying Armistice Day peace greetings and goodwill to American youth.
subfiles.summary: Seinan Boy Scouts' Armistice Day address pledges solidarity with youth worldwide and goodwill to American youth.
subfiles.title: Address presented by the Seinan Boy Scouts on Armistice Day
